newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Makina Takim targets $46.6 mln 1997 turnover.
newsitem.headline: Turk Makina Takim targets $46.6 mln 1997 turnover.

text.p: Turkey's leading metal- and wood-working tools producer Makina Takim Endustrisi A.S. plans to increase its turnover to $46.6 million in 1997 from $26 million expected in 1996, a company official said.

"Our 1997 turnover target is $46.6 million, including $30 million to be earned from direct factory sales and the rest from our store chain Mr. Bricolage," Cavit Vardarlilar, general manager of the company, told Reuters.

The company opened its first Mr. Bricolage store under a franchising agreement with the French company in 1996 and plans to open two new ones in 1997, one of them under a franchising agreement with another Turkish company.
Vardarlilar said Makina Takim recorded 2.5 trillion lira of sales in 1996, five percent above target. The average value of the lira in 1996 was $1=96,154.
"In 1997 we aim to raise this amount to seven trillion lira (at an estimated average rate of $1=150,000) with the help of our store chain, new markets and new products," he said.
The shares of the company ended at 2,600 lira at noon on Friday, unchanged from Thursday's close.

The company began producing electrical and manual hand-tools in 1996, in addition to 20,000 different types of cutting and drilling tools. It controls 80 percent of the cutting tools market and 50 percent of the carpentry tools market in Turkey.
Vardarlilar said they had invested $3 million on modernisation projects last year and would continue such investments until 2000.
"We will spend $4 million on the project in 1997 and this will add up to $10 million by the year 2000," he said.
The projects aim to shorten delivery time to 30 days from the current 60-90 days, to attract new demand which normally goes to imported products because of the long delivery time.
Makina Takim's exports were $11 million in 1996, mainly to Germany, France and Italy and mostly under various German brands and some under its own brand.
Vardarlilar said the 1997 export target was $15 million, including some central Asian countries as new markets.
"We will expand our Mr. Bricolage store chain to the central Asian countries and the first step will come in 1997," he said.

Vardarlilar expects a better business environment in Turkey in 1997 than last year. He said the automotive sector, Makina Takim's main customer, which faced difficulties in 1996 due to weak demand, would recover in 1997.
"We do not rely only on the automotive sector. We sell our products to several other industries like furniture, forestry products, milling, aluminium processing and defence," he said.
"So we expect more pluses in 1997 than in 1996 when considering the industry as a whole, but we are not as optimistic about the general Turkish economy," he added.
